candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.background: U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary 2021–2025; California Attorney General 2017–2021 (filed 122 lawsuits against the first Trump administration); 24 years in the U.S. House. Advanced from the June 2026 top-two primary.

cost.label: Campaign centers affordability; negotiated Medicare drug prices 38–79% below list (Wikipedia)

health.label: Led multi-state defense of the ACA; ran Medicare drug-price negotiations as HHS Secretary (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Led 21-state coalition defending DACA; sued over border-wall emergency declaration (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Created CA environmental-justice bureau; repeatedly sued to block environmental rollbacks (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Directed HHS to expand abortion-related care access after Dobbs (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Would declare a state of emergency to fund 40,000 already-approved affordable units awaiting financing (CalMatters voter guide)

taxes.label: Supports progressive income tax and extending a higher rate on high earners to pay for schools (CalMatters voter guide)

safety.label: Mixed: voted for Prop 36 and would fully fund it, while backing court-mandated drug treatment to avoid jail (CalMatters voter guide)

candidates.now: U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services
priorities: Build more housing
Protect and expand health care
Keep fuel and utilities affordable

nullNotes.education: checked Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, CalMatters voter guide ('has not released any major education policy proposals')
nullNotes.democracy: checked Ballotpedia, Wikipedia, CalMatters voter guide; nothing documented

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.background: Author and former Fox News host; former adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron; runs on a 'Cali-ffordability' platform. Advanced from the June 2026 top-two primary.

cost.label: 'Cali-ffordability': blames regulation/taxation for high costs; deregulation platform (KEYT)

housing.label: Backed initiative barring private CEQA lawsuits and capping developer impact fees (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Would end taxpayer-funded healthcare for undocumented immigrants; no broader plan stated (KEYT)

climate.label: '$3 gas,' halve electric bills through energy deregulation (KEYT)

safety.label: Reverse prison closures, expand capacity, implement Prop 36 (KEYT)

health.label: Health platform: end state-provided Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants (CalMatters voter guide)

priorities: Lower taxes and cost of living
Immigration enforcement
Reduce regulation

nullNotes.education: checked campaign site, Ballotpedia, iVoterGuide (survey unanswered), CalMatters; only phonics and third-grade retention, which do not map to the axis
nullNotes.repro: checked Ballotpedia, iVoterGuide (survey unanswered), CalMatters voter guide; nothing documented

candidates.name: Jeff Frese
candidates.background: Small business owner and father from Contra Costa County who has no FEC candidate record and ran a locally focused campaign, arguing his opponent is preoccupied with national and international matters. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary against fourteen year incumbent Mark DeSaulnier in a district that has not elected a Republican in decades.
priorities: Stop deficit spending that drives up mortgage rates and prices
Cut red tape that makes building slow and expensive
Back the police and stop the fentanyl pipeline

cost.label: 'Stop the deficit spending that drives up mortgage rates and prices' (campaign site)

health.label: 'Cap insulin and cut prescription drug costs', a price intervention rather than a market competition remedy (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed: would 'ban Wall Street and hedge funds from buying up single-family homes, homes are for families, not portfolios', while also promising to 'cut the red tape that makes building slow and expensive, communities decide how they grow, not Washington' (campaign site)

taxes.label: 'Reward work, let people keep more of what they earn' and 'no federal tax on teachers' salaries' (campaign site)

education.label: 'Money to classrooms, not bureaucrats', 'parents in charge', and 'back to basics, literacy, math, and critical thinking' (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Back the police. Prosecute crime', plus 'get serious about fentanyl' and 'stop the fentanyl pipeline' (campaign site)

democracy.label: Mixed: would 'require voter ID for federal elections' and 'use paper ballots as the permanent audit trail', while also wanting to 'make Election Day a national holiday' (campaign site)

nullNotes.immigration: Checked his campaign site at freseforcongress.com, which has no immigration plank, his BallotReady stance list, and his iVoterGuide profile, which records 'did not answer' on every question including immigration. No immigration position documented.
nullNotes.climate: Checked the campaign site, which states no energy or climate position, his BallotReady stance list, whose nearest item is reducing wildfire risk through federal forest management, and his iVoterGuide profile marked 'did not answer'. Forest management alone does not place him on the clean energy transition versus expanded production axis.
nullNotes.repro: Checked the campaign site, which has no abortion plank, his BallotReady stance list, and his iVoterGuide profile, which records 'did not answer' on the right to life section. No abortion position documented.

candidates.name: James Gallagher
candidates.background: Attorney and partner in his family's farming operation who served in the California State Assembly from 2014 and was Assembly Republican leader from 2022 to 2025. He won the June 2, 2026 special election with 62.1 percent to fill the vacancy left by Doug LaMalfa's death and took office that month. He also advanced from the concurrent top-two primary for the full term, against Democrat Mike McGuire.
priorities: Lower the cost of living through lower taxes, fees and regulation
Expand energy production to bring prices down
Tougher crime laws and continued border security

cost.label: Runs on 'expand energy production to bring prices down' and making life affordable 'through lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations' (campaign site)

health.label: Mixed: 'I think we do need to restore the Medi-Cal funding, but not for illegal immigrants', while calling seismic mandates on rural hospitals 'crazy' and urging 'reasonable things to cut their costs' (NSPR interview)

housing.label: 'You're never going to get there unless you reduce the input costs that go into market housing'; 'you have to remove those barriers that get in the way of building the project' (Chico News and Review)

immigration.label: Campaign pledge to 'continue the tough border security implemented by the President' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Campaign pledge to 'make life more affordable for North State families through lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations' (campaign site)

climate.label: 'The high gas prices in California are a result of California policy'; says 'you need to streamline the overly complicated environmental regulations' (Chico News and Review)

safety.label: Campaign pledge to 'enact tougher laws protect our communities, neighborhoods and homes from crime' (campaign site)

nullNotes.education: Checked the campaign site, which states no K-12 position, the Chico News and Review and NSPR primary interviews, and Ballotpedia, which records he filed no Candidate Connection survey in 2014, 2020, 2022 or 2024. His only education items are expanding community college vocational programs in nursing, logging and forestry, and a general parental rights line, neither of which maps onto the public investment versus school choice axis.
nullNotes.repro: Checked the campaign site, which states no abortion position, both 2026 primary interviews, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia. No abortion position is documented in this race.
nullNotes.democracy: Checked the campaign site, which states no elections position, both primary interviews and Ballotpedia. His only elections item is opposing partisan redistricting after Proposition 50, which is not a voting access or voter ID position and does not map onto this axis.

candidates.name: Mike McGuire
candidates.background: State senator for California's 2nd District since 2014 and president pro tempore of the State Senate from February 2024 until November 2025, the first North Coast senator to lead the chamber since 1866. He was elected to the Healdsburg School Board at 19 and later served on the city council and the Sonoma County Board of Supervisors. He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary to face Republican James Gallagher in November.
priorities: Pass Medicare for All and keep rural hospitals open
Lower costs for working families and take on corporate price gouging
Wildfire protection and doubling the CalFire firefighting force

cost.label: 'Lowering Costs for Working Families' plank: 'I'll raise wages, take on corporate price gouging, and fight to bring down the cost of living' (campaign issues)

health.label: 'Healthcare can't just be for the wealthy few'; 'In Congress, I'll fight to pass Medicare for All and keep rural hospitals open' (campaign issues)

housing.label: 'Tackling the Cost of Housing' plank backs affordable housing investments and renter protections (campaign issues)

immigration.label: Runs a 'Holding ICE Accountable' plank opposing what he calls the weaponization of government against Americans: 'I won't back down from that fight' (campaign issues)

taxes.label: 'Making Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share' plank: 'Here in California, I've made billionaires pay their fare share' and 'I've taken on big corporations and won' (campaign issues)

climate.label: 'Recognizes climate change for the existential threat that it is' and champions policies that reduce greenhouse gas emissions (official House site)

education.label: 'Values a public education, programs to support the whole child, accessible and affordable college opportunities'; the page states no support for vouchers or choice (official House site)

repro.label: 'Strong supporter of the Women's Health Protection Act, which blocks medically unnecessary abortion restrictions'; sponsors the Right to Contraception Act and the Access to Family Building Act (official House site)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act, which would require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, April 10, 2025 (House roll call 102)

nullNotes.safety: Checked his official House issues index, whose only public safety page is Gun Violence Prevention, plus Wikipedia, where the criminal justice material is a state bill requiring gun owners to report stolen weapons. The run book excludes gun stances from this axis, and nothing else places him on prevention versus enforcement.
